questions.prompt: Which values of local_filename were dangerous before the fix, and why?

points.text: A path instead of a plain file name.

evidence.quote: is a path instead of a plain filename.

points.text: For example "../escaped.jsonl" or an absolute path.
The file could be written outside the chosen folder.

questions.prompt: How does the new check tell a plain file name from a path?

points.text: A plain file name equals its own Path(...).name.
The empty string and ".." are refused explicitly.
The docstring now says it must be a plain filename.

evidence.quote: It must be a plain filename.

questions.prompt: What do the new tests check besides the ValueError?

points.text: Nothing is downloaded or written when the name is refused.

evidence.quote: The check happens before any download and nothing is written to disk.

points.text: The download function is mocked and must not be called.
Plain names that look odd, like ".hidden.jsonl", are still accepted.
